cues: The two are in parallel, so they have the same voltage: I g G equals I minus I g, times S.
So S equals I g G over I minus I g.
The finished ammeter has a very small resistance, G S over G plus S, because it goes in series, and must not disturb the current.
An ideal ammeter has zero resistance.
